title: Human acrocentric chromosome short-arm de novo mutation and recombination.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: ENA (European Nucleotide Archive) filereport for PRJEB86317: the read_run listing shows raw Oxford Nanopore WGS (whole-genome sequencing) runs of 2-36 GB each for CEPH pedigree samples (NA12877, NA12889-NA12892, ...); the analysis listing for the project is empty (no processed variant files deposited there). Europe PMC full text returned HTTP 500 and the supplement endpoint returned no zip.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 156 phased short arms, 107 transmissions from 23 samples, 18 q-arm recombination events, one ectopic recombination, a 10-fold elevated SNV (single-nucleotide variant) rate; all from the abstract. Whether de novo mutation calls are in a supplementary table is unknown.

a1_downloadable.note: Raw reads openly downloadable from ENA; no processed table found (checked ENA analysis listing; supplement not retrievable).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Any label (de novo mutation, recombination breakpoint) would have to be constructed by assembling and phasing raw long reads across a pedigree; no label table found in the files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Only raw sequencing reads in ENA; no assemblies or variant tables were found.

a4_units_stated.note: No tabular data located to check.

a5_enough_rows.note: 23 people, 107 transmissions, 18 recombination events per the abstract; de novo mutations on short arms likely only tens to low hundreds. Far below 400.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Hundreds of GB of raw nanopore reads (runs of 2-36 GB each, seen in ENA listing)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Raw sequencing over the size cap; assembly needs a cluster.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No processed counts available to compare.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels would be measured from sequencing (pedigree inheritance), not another model's output, but they do not exist as a table.

honest_claim_h3: Not applicable: a model trained on ~23 people's acrocentric de novo mutations could at most describe one family's mutation spectrum, not predict anything general.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence context on acrocentric chromosome short arms to predict where new mutations or crossovers arise in a family.
plain_idea.train_on: Sequence windows around de novo mutations or recombination breakpoints from one four-generation family; number of examples unknown but likely tens to low hundreds.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a position carries a new mutation or crossover, as observed by long-read sequencing of parents and children.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would show what drives the unusually high mutation rate on these repetitive chromosome arms, but too few events exist to train a model.

ml_idea: None viable: tiny event counts from one pedigree, available only as raw long reads.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; Part A failed on raw-only data and tiny n.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count rows in any supplementary de novo mutation table (expected under a few hundred).

verdict_reason: Only raw nanopore reads (hundreds of GB) in ENA for 23 pedigree members; labels must be constructed by assembly, and the event counts (18 recombinations, 107 transmissions) are far too small.
